newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Rivals factions clash on Liberia campaign trail.
newsitem.headline: Rivals factions clash on Liberia campaign trail.

text.p: Supporters of rival warlords-turned-politicians Charles Taylor and Alhaji Kromah have clashed with sticks and stones in the north eastern town of Ganta, a Taylor stronghold, witnesses said on Monday.
The clash, the fourth involving Taylor supporters in two weeks of campaigning for July 19 presidential and parliamentary elections, took place during an pre-election tour by Kromah.
"About 12 persons from both sides were injured by stones and stakes," one reporter travelling with Kromah said.

Kromah, arriving in Monrovia, blamed Taylor supporters and said such attacks could influence the election result in the area. "If these violent attacks go unpunished, we in the All Liberia Coalition Party (ALCOP) will not accept the election results from Nimba County," he added.
Supporters of a fresh delay in the election argue for an October poll, saying candidates cannot campaign freely.

"We must not allow elections under such conditions where one party will have an exclusive right to a particular part of this country," Samuel Kofi-Woods, head of the Catholic Justice and Peace Commission, said. "It is too early for an election that would be credible and democratic."

Liberia's West African neighbours, who brokered agreement on elections to end seven years of civil war, have already put them back from May. The war, launched by Taylor in 1989, has killed well over 150,000 people in the state set up by freed American slaves in 1847.
A Nigerian-led West African peacekeeping force, in Liberia since early in the war, disarmed many of its faction fighters and is providing election security.
